Level Switch Working Principle Compared With Other Point Level Switches

Level switch working principle is always the same idea: a sensor detects whether material is present at one fixed point and changes an ON or OFF contact. What differs between switch types is the physical effect used to sense the material. The membrane switch uses material pressure on a flexible diaphragm, while other designs use buoyancy, vibration damping, capacitance or rotation.

Level switch typeSensing principleTypical media
Membrane (diaphragm)Material pressure deflects a membrane that operates a microswitchPowders, granules, pellets
FloatBuoyancy lifts a float that moves a contact or magnetClean liquids
Vibrating forkFork vibration is damped or shifted in frequency when coveredLiquids and fine solids
CapacitanceCapacitance of the probe rises when material replaces airLiquids, slurries, solids
Rotary paddleA motor driven paddle stalls when buried in materialBulk solids in silos

Choosing the right principle

  1. Identify the medium: liquid, powder, granules or coarse solids.
  2. Check bulk density, because a membrane switch needs enough material pressure to deflect the diaphragm.
  3. Check temperature, abrasion and hygiene needs, which decide the membrane material.
  4. Decide the duty: high level alarm, low level alarm or overfill protection.
  5. Mount the switch on the vessel wall at the exact level point to be detected.

For dry bulk solids with moderate density, the membrane type gives a simple mechanical switch with few parts and low maintenance.
